question: At which point in the intra-operative sequence is the WHO Surgical Safety Checklist 'Sign Out' section completed?

answers.text: Before the patient is anaesthetised, to confirm the correct site and procedure

tipsAndFeedback.chosenFeedback: This describes 'Sign In' — the first check completed before induction of anaesthesia.

answers.text: After anaesthesia but before the skin incision, to confirm the team and equipment are ready

tipsAndFeedback.chosenFeedback: This describes 'Time Out' — the second check, performed with all team members present before the incision is made.

answers.text: Before the patient leaves the operating room, to confirm specimen labelling, equipment counts, and key concerns for recovery

tipsAndFeedback.chosenFeedback: Correct. 'Sign Out' is the third check, completed before the patient leaves theatre. It confirms instrument/swab counts, specimen labelling, and any concerns for the recovery team.

answers.text: On the ward the following morning, during the surgical team's post-operative round

tipsAndFeedback.chosenFeedback: The WHO checklist is completed intra-operatively. Post-operative review on the ward is a separate clinical process.

overallFeedback.feedback: Review the WHO Surgical Safety Checklist structure: Sign In (pre-anaesthesia), Time Out (pre-incision, all team present), Sign Out (before leaving theatre — counts, specimens, recovery handover).
Correct. The three WHO checklist stages are: Sign In (before anaesthesia) → Time Out (before incision) → Sign Out (before leaving theatre). Each targets a different set of preventable errors.
